text: Israel camped facing the tabernacle, not facing outward toward their enemies. God guarded their backs.
explanation:
"Everyone of the children of Israel shall camp by his own standard… around the tabernacle." Militarily it made no sense: an army keeps watch outward against attack. But God had all twelve tribes face inward, toward His dwelling. From above, the camp formed the shape of a cross.

That's the posture God wants for you. Don't spend your life scanning the horizon for every threat. Look to Jesus. "The glory of the Lord shall be your rear guard." When you keep your eyes on Him, He takes care of what comes from behind, and the enemy can't catch you by surprise.

text: The banners of the four leading tribes were a lion, an ox, a man and an eagle: the four faces of Jesus.
explanation:
Jewish tradition says Judah's banner on the east bore a lion, Reuben's on the south a man, Ephraim's on the west an ox, and Dan's on the north an eagle. They're the same four faces Ezekiel and John saw around God's throne, and they mirror the four Gospels: Matthew's King, Mark's tireless Servant, Luke's Son of Man, and John's Son of God who came from above.

When an army charged, it lifted its banner high. When the enemy comes against you, you don't have to turn and face every attack yourself. Lift up Jesus in praise, in testimony and in conversation. "Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered."

text: God placed the table of showbread on the north side, the direction Israel's invaders came from. Your answer to sickness is the Lord's Table.
explanation:
The four horsemen of Revelation 6 parallel what Jesus said in Matthew 24: false christs, wars, famines and pestilences. In everyday life they show up as false teaching, strife, lack and disease. And the tabernacle's furniture seems to answer each one. Scripture repeatedly says Israel's enemies came from the north, and the table of showbread stood on the north side.

Today that table is the Lord's Supper. When you discern His body, broken for your health, and His blood shed for your forgiveness, you're holding God's answer to pestilence and death. A table may look weak, but God's ordained ways are stronger than any weapon.

text: The lampstand stood on the south side of the tabernacle. Lampstands picture local churches, and God's answer to lack is there.
explanation:
John saw Jesus walking among seven golden lampstands, "the seven churches." In the tabernacle, the lampstand stood opposite the table, on the south side. It was fuelled by oil, a picture of the Holy Spirit filling the church with His gifts.

Of the early church it was written, "Great grace was upon them all. Nor was there anyone among them who lacked." Lack is one of the enemy's attacks, and part of God's answer is a local church: be planted in it, involved in it, and support it. Supply flows where His lampstand burns.

text: The altar of incense pictures prayer. The enemy isn't afraid of your strength. He fears you on your knees.
explanation:
The bronze altar, a picture of the cross, stands against false teaching: the message of Christ crucified exposes every substitute. The golden altar of incense stands for prayer, and Jesus Himself prays for us; when we pray in the Spirit, we join His intercession.

When the enemy stirs up strife in your home or church, the more you try to fix it in your own strength, the more he has to work with. But he can't stand an atmosphere of prayer. "The effective, fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much." Daniel's answer was sent the day he started praying, even though it took three weeks to arrive. Keep praying.

text: Each local church is called "the glory of Christ." No wonder the enemy keeps attacking it.
explanation:
Paul described the messengers of the churches as "the glory of Christ." On the high priest's breastplate, the gems bore the names of tribes, not individuals. Each stone flashed a different colour, and together they displayed the full beauty. Every local church reflects a ray of His glory that another doesn't; together they show all of it.

So when trouble or division hits your church, remember: it isn't ultimately about you. The devil is trying to tarnish Christ's glory. Don't take his bait. Stay rooted, keep Jesus at the centre, and as your church comes through the trial, His light will shine even brighter.

text: God described creation in one chapter. He spent about fifteen on the tabernacle, which pictures His Son, and repeated much of it. He never tires of talking about Jesus.
explanation:
Moses spent forty days on the mountain while God described the tabernacle in loving detail; only at the end did He hand over the tablets of stone. Then, chapters later, much of it is repeated almost word for word. Is it redundant? Not to a Father who delights in His Son. Every board, curtain and colour speaks of Jesus.

When Joseph revealed himself to his brothers, he said, "Tell my father of all my glory in Egypt." That's worship: telling the Father about the glory you see in His Son. So talk about Jesus to your children, your spouse and your friends. The more you see of Him, the richer your worship becomes.
